scripts.//verify:out: Is out/ built from the source on disk? firebase.json points hosting at zipper-crm/out, so a deploy ships that directory — not git, and not whatever the last build printed. Checks freshness, probes the bundle for strings that were deleted and added, and prints artifact hashes. Run it after `npm run build` and before any hosting deploy.
scripts.//test:routing: The partner redirect table. `lib/partnerRouting.ts` has no imports and no React on purpose, so the real module compiles and runs standalone — the spec exercises the shipped code, not a copy of it.
scripts.test:routing: rm -rf .routing-test && tsc lib/partnerRouting.ts lib/partnerRouting.spec.ts --outDir .routing-test --module commonjs --target ES2020 --strict --moduleResolution node --esModuleInterop && node .routing-test/partnerRouting.spec.js; code=$?; rm -rf .routing-test; exit $code
scripts.//test:session: The session gate — the only thing that may send somebody to /login. `lib/sessionGate.ts` has no imports and no React on purpose, so the real module compiles and runs standalone and the spec exercises shipped code.
scripts.test:session: rm -rf .session-test && tsc lib/sessionGate.ts lib/sessionGate.spec.ts --outDir .session-test --module commonjs --target ES2020 --strict --moduleResolution node --esModuleInterop && node .session-test/sessionGate.spec.js; code=$?; rm -rf .session-test; exit $code
scripts.//test:appeals: What an appeal status means, and who it may be attributed to. `lib/appealStatus.ts` has no imports and no React on purpose, so the real module compiles and runs standalone. scripts.test:appeals: rm -rf .appeals-test && tsc lib/appealStatus.ts lib/appealStatus.spec.ts --outDir .appeals-test --module commonjs --target ES2020 --strict --moduleResolution node --esModuleInterop && node .appeals-test/appealStatus.spec.js; code=$?; rm -rf .appeals-test; exit $code

scripts.test:secondrole: rm -rf .secondrole-test && tsc lib/secondRoleRule.ts lib/secondRoleHeld.spec.ts --outDir .secondrole-test --module commonjs --target ES2020 --strict --moduleResolution node --esModuleInterop && node .secondrole-test/secondRoleHeld.spec.js; code=$?; rm -rf .secondrole-test; exit $code
scripts.//test:crmroles: Who the /users list may offer moderation actions against. `lib/crmRoles.ts` has no imports and no React on purpose, so the real module compiles and runs standalone. Re-run whenever an avatar is added, renamed or redrawn in zipper-app.
scripts.//test:photo: Resolving a stored photoUrl. `lib/profilePhoto.ts` has no React and no Firebase on purpose, so the real module runs standalone. Guards the one that bit us: `avatar:fox` is not a URL, and every CRM surface put it straight into .

scripts.//test:hooks: Rules of Hooks, over every component in the CRM. The agency dashboard had a useMemo and a useSecureThumbs below three conditional returns, so the hook COUNT changed between the loading render and the loaded one and React threw "Rendered more hooks than during the previous render" — which Next's GlobalError shows as "Application error: a client-side exception has occurred". The whole dashboard, blank, for every agency owner. Nothing caught it: it typechecks, it builds, and it only fails on the second render. --no-inline-config because this config loads the hooks plugin only, and the files carry eslint-disable comments for rules it does not know.
